title: Cycle Slate Sculpting and Emergency Bump Protocol
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Objective: Create a pragmatic playbook that operations, PMs, and Eng leads can use during cycle planning and mid-cycle stress to (1) rapidly sculpt the committed slate to fit available capacity, (2) define an "emergency bump" mechanism for time-limited role augmentation, and (3) formalize decision rights and rollback criteria so downstream teams (DX, Sales, SRE) get predictable signals.

Background: We consistently see two failure modes: optimistic slate commits that erode quality when key contributors are pulled, and ad-hoc mid-cycle staffing swaps that create churn. Current artifacts (ad-hoc spreadsheets, Slack partial approvals) are noisy and lack clear thresholds for triggering de-prioritization vs. surge. This playbook is intended to be operational from day 0 of the cycle.

Scope:
- Runbook for PMs and Eng managers to prune scope with measurable impact estimates (dev hours, regression risk).
- Emergency bump policy that defines when and how to apply 1-2 sprint 'bump' FTEs (shadow or contractor) including approval flow and budget tagging.
- Role benchmarking matrix: mapping common task archetypes (infra, runtime, SDK, console) to skill-bands and expected throughput so swaps are comparable.
- Communication templates (stakeholder notice, release note, customer-impact table).
- Automation hooks: lightweight spreadsheet -> Google Sheet templates + a short script to surface candidates for bumping, and an optional GitHub label workflow to flag bumped PRs.

Success metrics: 
- Reduce cycle mid-sprint scope churn by 35% vs. last three cycles (measured by closed-in-cycle scope additions/removals).
- Mean time to decision for emergency bump < 48 hours.
- 80% of bumped activities have a documented rollback or handoff plan.

Constraints & Trade-offs:
- We prefer quick, conservative decisions rather than heavy analysis; the runbook emphasizes heuristics and guardrails (e.g., max 10% of sprint capacity for emergency bumps).
- Bumping external contractors increases cost but reduces risk of cross-feature regressions; include finance signaling.
- Avoid centralizing all bump approvals; propose two-tier authority (Eng Director for >1 FTE equivalent; PM + Eng Manager pair for <=1).

Stakeholders: PMs (product-management), Eng leads (engineering), Design (as required for UX changes), Finance, People Ops (for contractor onboarding), Solutions/Support for customer comms.

Artifacts: PRD draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cEXAMPLE_PRD, runbook spreadsheet template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1exampleSheet, sample GitHub automation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4312

Next steps: Align stakeholder reps week of 2026-03-15, pilot with Cycle 2026-W12 planning, and iterate based on two pilot teams (Runtime and Console).
acceptance_criteria: Runbook published in Confluence with step-by-step decision flow and one-sentence rationale for each fork
Google Sheet template populated and tested with two pilot teams
Approval flow documented and two approvers named (Eng Director + PM lead) with contact templates
Automation stub (GH label + sheet exporter) merged to infra-tools repo
Post-pilot retrospective scheduled and success metrics baseline captured
